8.title: The Infinite Spirit
8.b0.ask: “Is the Holy Spirit just an influence, or a being with personality?”
8.b2.p: In Paper 6 we met the Eternal Son, God the Word. God is the thought, the Son is the word, and the Spirit is the act — in this paper that sentence is finally complete. For here the Third Person of Deity, the Infinite Spirit, comes onto the stage.
8.b3.p: The Infinite Spirit is often called the Holy Spirit, and many people think of him not as a person but as a widespread influence — an atmosphere, a kind of energy. Paper 8 takes on this misunderstanding directly. The One who is present everywhere and does countless works is, for all that, a true and divine person, just as the Father and the Son are.
8.b7.p: When the Infinite Spirit was personalized, the circle of divine personality was at last complete. His first act was to fully recognize his divine parents, the Father and the Son. And of his own free will, though he is equal with the First and Second Persons, he pledged eternal loyalty to the Father and acknowledged everlasting dependence on the Son.
8.b8.p: This mutual recognition and willing devotion established the Paradise Trinity. If the Father is the initiating thought and the Son the word that expresses it, the Spirit is the one who carries that thought and word out in real action. That is why the first section of this paper is called “⟦Q 8:1.1|8:1.3|8:1.4⟧The God of Action.⟦/Q⟧”
8.b9.t: The initiating thought — the First Source from which all things come
The expressing word — the divine expression that reveals the thought perfectly
The accomplishing act — the executive who turns thought and word into actual creation
8.b11.p: No single name can hold the whole of the Infinite Spirit. The Universal Spirit, the Conjoint Creator, the Divine Executive, the Infinite Mind, the Paradise Mother Spirit, the Conjoint Actor, the Omnipresent Spirit — each of these many names shows one side of what he does.
8.b12.p: The Infinite Spirit fully shares the Father’s perfection, righteousness, and love, yet he especially inclines toward the merciful attributes of the Son. So he becomes the minister of mercy of the Paradise Deities to the grand universe.
8.b13.t: A co-worker with the Father and the Son in building the universe
The one who turns thought and word into real action
The source of mind that upholds every intelligent being
The one who is present everywhere and embraces all spirits
A motherly nature that cares for and nurtures
8.b14.h: 3. Relation of the Spirit to the Father and the Son
8.b15.p: Since the Third Person was personalized, the Father no longer takes part personally in creation. Instead he delegates everything possible to the Son, and the Son in turn passes on all possible authority and power to the Infinite Spirit. This chain of delegation, flowing from above downward, is how the universe we live in came to be built.
8.b17.p: So at the center of all things, the Infinite Spirit is the first of the Paradise Deities whom ascending pilgrims reach. Because the Third Person enshrouds the Second and the First, all who seek to come to the Son and the Father must first meet the Spirit.
8.b18.t: The order in which ascenders meet them
The first to be recognized — the Third Person, who enshrouds the other two
The Second Person, reached through the Spirit
The First Source, approached at last through the Son
8.b21.p: Unceasing ministry to mind is the very nature of the Infinite Spirit. In the Creative Spirits of each local universe — the Mother Spirits — we see the Infinite Spirit devoted to raising material creatures to ever higher levels of spiritual attainment.
8.b22.p: The Spirit does not humble himself as the Son does, by coming down in the flesh. But the Infinite Spirit and his co-ordinate Spirits step themselves down, joyfully passing through a long series of divinity attenuations, until at last they appear as angels to stand by our side and guide us through the lowly paths of earthly life.
8.b23.t: How he comes down to us
Incarnation — he comes down himself, taking on a mortal body
Divinity attenuation — he steps himself down and appears as angels who guide us at our side
8.b25.p: The outstanding attribute of the Infinite Spirit is omnipresence. The presence of this spirit, which pervades the whole universe, is very much like the presence of a universal and divine mind.
8.b26.p: The phrase “⟦Q 8:5.3|8:5.5|8:5.6⟧Spirit of God⟦/Q⟧” refers to two things together: the Infinite Spirit on Paradise himself, and the Creative Spirit belonging to each local universe, whose spiritual circuit is the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit is confined to its own local universe, but the Infinite Spirit is everywhere.
8.b27.t: Omnipresent — present everywhere in all the universes
The Creative Spirit of a local universe (the Holy Spirit)
Confined — active only within that local universe
8.b29.p: This is the place the whole paper has been heading toward. The Infinite Spirit is a universe presence, an eternal action, a cosmic power, a holy influence, and a universal mind. He is all of these and infinitely more — but he is also a true and divine personality.
8.b30.p: The Infinite Spirit has absolute mind, he has will, he loves, and he can be grieved. That is why the words “⟦Q 8:6.4⟧Grieve not the Spirit of God⟦/Q⟧” are literally true. An influence cannot grieve. Only a person grieves, loves, and speaks.
8.b31.t: “⟦Q 8:6.3⟧The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.⟦/Q⟧”
He loves and can be grieved
“⟦Q 8:6.4⟧He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says.⟦/Q⟧” · “⟦Q 8:6.4⟧The Spirit himself makes intercession for you.⟦/Q⟧”
“⟦Q 8:6.4⟧For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.⟦/Q⟧”
8.b34.p: From beginning to end, Paper 8 answers a single question. Is this all-present something we call the Holy Spirit merely an energy or an atmosphere? Or is he a person who knows me, who grieves with me, and who intercedes for me? The text answers clearly: he is a person.
8.b36.t: The Spirit turns the Father’s thought and the Son’s word into real action
Each of his many names shows one side of what he does
3. Relation of the Spirit to the Father and the Son
Only through the Spirit do we reach the Son, and only through the Son the Father
God is love, the Son is mercy, the Spirit is ministry
The Holy Spirit is confined to the local universe, but the Infinite Spirit is everywhere
Not an influence, but a true person who loves and can be grieved
9.title: Relation of the Infinite Spirit to the Universe
9.b0.ask: “How does an unseen Spirit hold the whole universe together?”
9.b2.p: In Paper 8 we learned that the Infinite Spirit is not a pervasive influence but a true person. Paper 9 moves on to the next question: how does this personal Spirit actually relate to the vast universe?
9.b3.p: He manipulates energy, he bestows mind, and he knows at once what is happening on worlds far away. Yet none of this activity blurs his personality. On the contrary, every one of these deeds is the volitional act of a single person.
9.b6.h: 1. Attributes of the Third Source and Center
9.b7.p: No single name can hold the Infinite Spirit. As God the Spirit, he is the personality co-ordinate and divine equal of the Father and the Son. As the Infinite Spirit, he is an omnipresent spiritual influence. As the God of Action, he is the apparent ancestor of motion and change (9:1.1).
9.b8.p: Some of his attributes come from the Father and some from the Son, while still others are found in neither — they belong to the Third Source and Center alone (9:1.2). Each of the three persons upholds the universe in a different way.
9.b9.t: Infinite in love and volition — the universal upholder
Infinite in wisdom and truth — the universal revealer
Infinite in synthesis — the universal unifier
9.b11.p: God is spirit in a threefold sense. He himself is spirit; in his Son he appears as spirit without qualification; and in the Conjoint Actor he appears as spirit allied with mind (9:2.1).
9.b12.p: The Infinite Spirit is just as much a complement of the Eternal Son as the Son is of the Father. The Eternal Son is a spiritualized personalization of the Father; the Infinite Spirit is a personalized spiritualization of both the Son and the Father (9:2.2).
9.b13.t: The very nature of God the Father
Spirit as it appears in the Eternal Son
Spirit as it appears in the Conjoint Actor, the Infinite Spirit
9.b15.p: Paradise is the source of physical gravity. But the Infinite Spirit possesses a unique power found in neither the Father nor the Son: antigravity. This ability to withstand the pull of material gravity belongs to the Third Source and Center alone (9:3.2).
9.b17.p: In Paper 7 we learned about material gravity and spirit gravity. Now a third kind is added: the gravity of mind. Only where all three work together is a whole creature fashioned.
9.b18.t: Comes from Paradise and holds all material reality
Comes from the Eternal Son and draws all spiritual reality
Comes from the Infinite Spirit and holds every being that has mind
9.b20.p: The Third Source and Center has an intellectual nature distinct from his physical and spiritual attributes. This mind belongs neither to energy nor to pure spirit; it works in the place where the two meet (9:4.2).
9.b21.p: The Conjoint Creator is absolute only in the domain of mind. The mind endowment of the seven superuniverses comes from the Seven Master Spirits, his primary personalities (9:4.3).
9.b22.t: Thing — the material stuff of the universe
Meaning — the work of intellect that lets us understand things
Value — what is true, beautiful, and good within the meaning
9.b24.p: Because the Third Person is the source of mind, evolving will creatures find it easier to form ideas of the Infinite Spirit than of either the Eternal Son or the Universal Father (9:5.4). The mind we use every day is itself the point of contact.
9.b25.p: But the paper quickly adds a careful balance. The fact that mind has a divine source does not make every happening of mind divine. Our intellect is still rooted in our animal origins, and we can mar it by insincerity and unrighteousness (9:5.5–7).
9.b26.t: Two things to remember about mind
The source of mind is divine
The Conjoint Creator is the bestower of mind, and its origin is holy (9:5.2)
Mind itself is not an object of worship
The Conjoint Creator is the source of mind, but mind is not the Conjoint Creator (9:5.5)
9.b28.p: The Conjoint Actor exercises a drawing power on all minds. All true and genuine intellectual values, all divine thoughts, are drawn into this absolute circuit of mind (9:6.2).
9.b29.p: Yet personality itself does not come from spirit, mind, or matter. The dignity of personal selfhood is the bestowal of the Universal Father alone (9:6.4). Mind is the place where personality grows, but it is not the power that creates personality.
9.b30.t: The perfect expression of the Creator’s mind
The evolving expression of the minds of all creatures toward their Creator
9.b32.p: The Conjoint Actor co-ordinates all things — mental, material, and spiritual — so that they can be known at the same moment. This is reflectivity: the unique and inexplicable power to see, hear, sense, and know all that happens throughout a superuniverse, and to focus it all at any chosen point (9:7.1).
9.b33.p: Spirit traces back to the Son, physical energy to Paradise, and mind to the Third Source and Center; but reflectivity is a unique union of all three (9:7.2). That is how the rulers of the universe can know about faraway conditions instantly, as if they were there.
9.b34.t: From the Third Source and Center
9.b36.p: The Infinite Spirit has full power to pass on many of his powers and prerogatives to co-ordinate and subordinate personalities (9:8.1). In this way the vast family of the Third Source and Center serves throughout the universe.
9.b37.p: The spirit personalities of this divine family are forever dedicated to ministering the love of God and the mercy of the Son to the evolving worlds of time and space. They are the living ladder on which mortal man climbs from chaos to glory (9:8.25).
9.b38.t: The Seven Master Spirits of Paradise · the Reflective Spirits of the superuniverses · the Creative Spirits of the local universes
Control creatures who oversee physical forces throughout all organized space
The Personalities of the Infinite Spirit
The higher personalities · the messenger hosts of space · the ministering spirits of time
9.b40.box: The Conjoint Creator manipulates energy and is the source of mind, yet at the root of all his activity there is always the volitional act of one person.
9.b41.p: Paper 9 is not simply a list of what the Infinite Spirit does. Whether he is using antigravity, bestowing mind, or knowing at once what happens on distant worlds, the paper shows that all of this is not a scattering of separate powers but one activity flowing from one person.
9.b43.t: Attributes of the Third Source and Center
The three persons uphold the universe each in a different way
The Infinite Spirit is the personalized spiritualization of the Father and the Son
After material and spirit gravity, mind gravity is added as a third
Energy is thing, mind is meaning, spirit is value
The source of mind is divine, but mind itself is not to be worshiped
Personality comes not from mind but from the Father alone
Spirit, energy, and mind unite so that distant things are known at once
A vast spirit family forms the ladder of ascent
10.title: The Paradise Trinity
10.b0.ask: “Why did the perfect Father not remain alone, but form a Trinity?”
10.b2.p: The Trinity is not a teaching that divides God. Rather, because the Father freely gave away his infinite power and personality to the Son and the Spirit, holding nothing back that could be given, he is not locked up alone as an absolute. He is able to exist eternally as one together with the Son and the Spirit.
10.b3.p: Paper 10 explains how this sharing came about, how the three can be one, and how that oneness reaches out to us finite creatures — and even to realities beyond the finite.
10.b6.h: 1. Self-Distribution of the First Source and Center
10.b7.p: Back in eternity, the Father began a policy of profound self-distribution. Everything that could be delegated he handed over to his Sons and their associated intelligences. As a result, the Father bestows the “⟦Q 10:1.4|10:2.5⟧personality of infinity⟦/Q⟧” upon the Son, while the Father and the Son together bestow the “conjoint personality” of their eternal union upon the Infinite Spirit (10:1.2, 1.4).
10.b8.p: Self-distribution is not a loss. It is the way of love that divine free will chose for itself. The more the Father gave, the more fully he became the Father.
10.b9.t: The “conjoint personality” of their eternal union
Every power and all authority that could be delegated
10.b11.p: By the technique of trinitization the Father set the Son apart from himself — and by that very act he became a Father. The Father, the Son, and the Spirit are each unique persons, and at the same time they are wholly united (10:2.6).
10.b12.p: With the appearance of the Third Source and Center, the existential cycle of Deity personalization was complete.
10.b13.t: The conjoint personality of the Father and the Son
10.b15.p: There is only one Deity, yet Deity actively functions as three persons. Outside of Havona, in the universes of time and space, the First Source and Center makes himself known in seven different ways (10:3.9–16).
10.b16.p: The Son functions as a person only in the domain of the spiritual universe, while the Spirit works universally in the spheres of mind, matter, and spirit.
10.b17.t: Through the Creator Sons, his grandsons
Through the gravity center of Paradise
Through his exclusive fragments — in mortal man, the Thought Adjusters
10.b19.p: The Trinity is an association that functions in a nonpersonal way, but never against personality. The Father, Son, and Spirit act not only as the Trinity; as persons they can also collaborate freely as they choose — but that collaboration is not the Trinity (10:4.4).
10.b20.p: The distinction is subtle but important. The action of the Trinity and the personal co-operation of the three persons belong to different levels.
10.b21.t: Father, Son, and Spirit function as one Deity union
They work together freely as individual persons, but not as the Trinity
10.b23.p: The personal Deities have attributes, but it is better to think of the Trinity in terms of functions rather than attributes — such as justice administration, totality attitudes, and cosmic overcontrol (10:5.1).
10.b24.p: The Trinity holds three attitudes at once, depending on the level with which it is dealing.
10.b25.t: Its maximum self-limitation — the “⟦Q 10:5.4|10:7.3|0:8.10⟧Trinity of Supremacy⟦/Q⟧”
More than finite but less than absolute — the “⟦Q 10:5.5|10:8.2|106:8.9⟧Trinity of Ultimacy⟦/Q⟧”
Culminating in the action of total Deity
10.b26.h: 6. The Stationary Sons of the Trinity
10.b27.p: All law takes origin in the Father; its administration belongs to the Son, and its revelation and interpretation to the Spirit. But the application of law — justice — is carried out by certain Sons of the Trinity. Justice is never the attitude of one person acting alone; it is always a plural function (10:6.2).
10.b28.p: This group of Trinity Sons includes the following ten orders. The author of the paper himself belongs to the tenth, the Universal Censors (10:6.16).
10.b29.t: Order of the Stationary Sons of the Trinity
10.b31.p: The Father, Son, and Spirit are truly one. Yet as things appear on the finite level, the Paradise Trinity is concerned not with parts but only with the whole (10:7.2).
10.b32.p: The Supreme Being reflects the attitude of the Trinity, but because he is still incomplete, we cannot fully predict the overcontrol of Supremacy. Still, as time passes, we see that all difficult and mysterious situations work out for the welfare and progress of the universes (10:7.5).
10.b33.t: As a whole, not in parts
As a whole, not in parts
As a whole, not in parts
As a whole, not in parts
10.b35.p: The Trinity also functions in ways that transcend the finite. The Ultimate is a qualified manifestation of the Trinity in relation to the absonite, just as the Supreme partially represents the Trinity in relation to the finite (10:8.2).
10.b36.p: We know the Father, the Son, and the Spirit as persons, but the author does not personally know the Deity Absolute. Only infinity can disclose the Father-Infinite (10:8.9).
10.b37.t: The Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit
Known, loved, and worshiped as persons
Not known personally, yet respected and honored
Wholly unfathomable, and growing ever more so
10.b40.p: Paper 10 does not leave the Trinity as a riddle to be solved. Because the Father shared himself, the Son and the Spirit exist; and because the three are one, there is perfect unity of purpose and oneness of execution in all the activities of the universe. We who are finite cannot know the full absoluteness of the Trinity, but as we ascend, we will again and again experience with astonishment new revelations of its supremacy and ultimacy.
10.b41.t: Self-Distribution of the First Source and Center
The more the Father gave, the more fully he became the Father
Each of the three is unique, yet all are wholly united
The one God functions in seven different ways
The union of the Trinity differs from personal collaboration
The Trinity is understood by its functions, not its attributes
The Stationary Sons of the Trinity
Justice is always a plural function
The Trinity is always concerned with the whole, not the parts
Only infinity can disclose the Father-Infinite
11.title: The Eternal Isle of Paradise
11.b0.ask: “Is the place where God dwells really somewhere?”
11.b2.p: Paper 10 showed how the three Deities work together as one. Paper 11 shows the place where those three dwell. The very first sentences are clear: Paradise is the eternal center of the universe of universes, and it is a material sphere as well as a spiritual abode (11:0.1).
11.b3.p: Why must it be material? Because all of the Father’s intelligent creation lives on material abodes, the absolute center that holds it all together must also be a literal, real place (11:0.1). Of its origin there are neither records nor traditions; Paradise is from eternity (11:0.2). The Perfector of Wisdom who presents this paper describes, one after another, its shape and regions, and the space and gravity that come from it. At the end he leads us to ask: what does this place have to do with me?
11.b7.p: Paradise serves many purposes, but to creatures it is above all the home of Deity. At the very center of the upper surface of this nearly circular, but not spherical, abode is the personal presence of the Universal Father. The Eternal Son immediately surrounds him, and both are invested by the glory of the Infinite Spirit (11:1.1). God dwells, has dwelt, and will forever dwell in this same place (11:1.2).
11.b8.p: The author uses the example of cities on a map. A city like New York or Rome does not cease to exist because you have never visited it. In the same way, the fact that few creatures have yet reached Paradise does not make God’s residence any less real. Given the time and means of passage, spiritual qualification, and guidance, anyone could journey inward from universe to universe and circuit to circuit until at last standing before the Father (11:1.3).
11.b9.p: The Father is always to be found at this center. If he moved, universal pandemonium would follow, for the lines of gravity from the ends of creation all converge in him (11:1.4). Whichever line we follow, the author says, we arrive at the same place (11:1.4).
11.b10.t: What we can follow along it
Ascending personalities journeying inward to the Father
The insurging cycles of cosmic force flowing to nether Paradise
The inward processional of the Paradise Sons toward the Eternal Son
The trillions of celestial beings who spring from the Infinite Spirit
11.b11.p: Whether we follow one of these lines or all of them, we are led straight back to the Father’s central abode. From there the flood-streams of life, energy, and personality flow out to all universes (11:1.4).
11.b13.p: So vast a material universe must have a capital worthy of the dignity of its Ruler (11:2.1). Yet this capital differs in shape from the planets we know (11:2.2).
11.b14.t: Not spherical but definitely ellipsoid, and essentially flat
One-sixth longer than the east-west diameter
One tenth of the east-west diameter
11.b15.p: These differences in dimension, together with the Isle’s stationary status and the greater force-energy pressure at its north end, make it possible to establish absolute direction in the master universe (11:2.3). Geographically the Isle is divided into three domains of activity (11:2.4–8).
11.b16.t: The plane of personality activities, seemingly dominated by the Trinity
Activities that are neither strictly personal nor nonpersonal
The impersonal plane, where the functional space presence of the Unqualified Absolute is focused
11.b17.p: The substance of the Isle is a single form of materialization found nowhere else in the universe. The Melchizedeks of Nebadon named it absolutum. It is neither dead nor alive; it is the original nonspiritual expression of the First Source and Center (11:2.9). The Father seems to have concentrated all absolute potential for cosmic reality in Paradise as part of freeing himself from the limitations of infinity, so that finite creation could become possible (11:2.10).
11.b18.p: This does not mean that Paradise is bound by time and space. Paradise exists without time and has no location in space (11:2.10). Rather, time and space seem to begin near Paradise (11:2.11).
11.b20.p: The citizens of the central Isle do not live in time as we know it, though they are fully conscious of a nontime sequence of events. Motion there is not inherent; it is volitional (11:2.11).
11.b22.p: On upper Paradise there are three grand spheres of activity (11:3.1).
11.b23.t: The center where the presence of the Deities dwells
Worship, trinitization, and high spiritual attainment; no material structures
The outlying residential region, divided into seven concentric zones
11.b24.p: The Most Holy Sphere is wholly spiritual, and the author admits that it is useless to try to describe its beauty to us, who are almost wholly material (11:3.1). In the Holy Land sectors, however, there are many souvenirs of our material days (11:3.2).
11.b25.p: Paradise is called “⟦Q 11:3.3|159:5.16|171:4.7⟧the Father’s House,⟦/Q⟧” and the seven zones of the Holy Area are often called “⟦Q 11:3.3⟧the Father’s Paradise mansions⟦/Q⟧” (11:3.3). The residents of the two inner zones are described.
11.b26.t: Paradise Citizens and natives of Havona dwelling on Paradise
Natives of the seven superuniverses; divided into seven sectors that are the Paradise home of ascendant creatures
11.b27.p: Each sector is divided into residential units, and the scale at which these units combine is almost too great to follow in numbers (11:3.4).
11.b28.t: Through supersuperior, celestial, and supercelestial units to the supreme units
11.b29.p: And yet all of this occupies considerably less than one per cent of the assigned area of the Holy Land. There is plenty of room left — not only for those now on their way inward, but even for those who will not start the Paradise climb until the distant future (11:3.4).
11.b31.p: The Isle ends abruptly at its edge, but it is so enormous that the angle of that edge cannot be noticed (11:4.1). This periphery is the landing and dispatching field for spirit personalities. Because the zones of unpervaded space nearly touch the periphery, all transports bound for Paradise land here. Neither upper nor nether Paradise can be approached by transport supernaphim (11:4.1).
11.b32.p: The Seven Master Spirits also keep force-focal headquarters here, and the presences of the Seven Supreme Power Directors mark the seven flash stations that send energies out to the seven superuniverses (11:4.2). Here too are the enormous historic and prophetic exhibit areas assigned to the Creator Sons (11:4.3).
11.b33.t: Exactly seven trillion now set up or in reserve (11:4.3)
About four per cent of the peripheral area so assigned (11:4.3)
Area in use by the existing universes
From one to four per cent (11:4.4)
Area assigned compared with actual need
At least one million times greater (11:4.4)
11.b34.p: The author infers that this unused land is reserved for creations that will someday exist beyond the seven superuniverses (11:4.3). Then he stops trying to describe it further. We must wait, he says, and ascend while we wait (11:4.5).
11.b37.p: About nether Paradise, the author first explains that we know only what has been revealed. No personalities sojourn there, and it has nothing to do with the affairs of spirit intelligences. Yet all physical-energy and cosmic-force circuits have their origin there (11:5.1). It is arranged as follows (11:5.2–4).
11.b38.t: The unknown and unrevealed Zone of Infinity
The outer margins of the under surface
A region of space potency and force-energy — a vast elliptical force center
11.b39.p: This force center at the outer margins is made up of three concentric elliptical zones (11:5.4).
11.b40.t: The focal point of the force-energy activities of Paradise itself; it acts like a gigantic heart whose pulsations direct and modify force (11:5.5)
Expands and contracts through three cycles; its function is not identified, but it seems to adjust between the inner and outer zones (11:5.6)
The largest and most active; believed to be the central focus of the space presence of the Unqualified Absolute (11:5.7)
11.b41.p: The force of the inner zone seems to flow in at the south and out at the north. It does not respond to observable physical gravity, but it is always obedient to Paradise gravity (11:5.5). The mid-zone pulsates in three ways (11:5.6).
11.b42.t: In every direction — a general expansion and contraction
11.b43.p: The outer zone breathes in only one direction at a time. For a little more than one billion Urantia years its space-force is outgoing; then for a similar length of time it is incoming (11:5.8). All physical force, energy, and matter are one; they proceed from nether Paradise and return there after completing their space circuit. Space itself, however, does not originate there. Space is not force, energy, or power (11:5.9).
11.b45.p: Here again the author is frank. We do not know the actual mechanism of space respiration; we only observe that all space alternately contracts and expands (11:6.1). To picture its shape, think of an hourglass. There are two kinds of space.
11.b46.t: Extends horizontally; where the universes are
Approaching the mid-point of the expanding phase (11:6.4)
Extends vertically; the reservoirs above and below Paradise
Nearing the mid-point of the contracting phase (11:6.4)
11.b47.p: As the universes expand, the reservoirs contract, and the reverse. The two kinds of space meet just underneath nether Paradise, where they pass through regulation channels that change one into the other (11:6.2). “Unpervaded” space means space not pervaded by the forces, energies, powers, and presences known to exist in pervaded space (11:6.3).
11.b48.p: Each phase lasts a little more than one billion Urantia years, and a full cycle of expansion and contraction takes a little over two billion years (11:6.4–5). The admission that we do not even know whether there is a creative intent concerning unpervaded space (11:6.3) shows that the revelation does not claim to know everything.
11.b50.p: Space does not exist on any surface of Paradise. Looking straight up from the upper surface, one would see nothing but unpervaded space, just now coming in. Space does not touch Paradise; only the quiet midspace zones are in contact with the Isle (11:7.1). Paradise is the motionless nucleus of these quiet zones (11:7.2).
11.b51.p: A vertical cross section of total space would slightly resemble a Maltese cross (11:7.3).
11.b52.t: The quiet midspace zones, which grow larger with distance until they enclose all space
11.b53.p: Space is neither the Unqualified Absolute nor a function of the Ultimate; it is a bestowal of Paradise (11:7.4). Pervaded space takes the shape of a V-shaped plane revolving around the Isle (11:7.5), and it thickens with distance from Paradise somewhat faster than the plane of the universes does (11:7.6).
11.b54.p: The quiet zones between the space levels separate the vast galaxies that race around Paradise (11:7.7–8). Even the alternating clockwise and counterclockwise flow of the galaxies is by design. It keeps gravity pressure from building to a destructive point and acts as a brake on dangerous velocities (11:7.9).
11.b56.p: Gravity is the all-powerful grasp of the physical presence of Paradise. The author calls it the omnipotent strand on which the stars, suns, and spheres are strung (11:8.1). The center of absolute material gravity is the Isle of Paradise, complemented by the dark gravity bodies encircling Havona and balanced by the space reservoirs above and below (11:8.2).
11.b57.p: Space does not respond to gravity, but it acts as a counterweight to it. Without the cushion of space, explosive action would jerk the surrounding bodies (11:8.3).
11.b58.t: Belongs to the electrical stage of energy or matter, and operates wherever materialization has taken place
11.b59.p: Cosmic force, energy, and matter fall into three stages according to how they respond to Paradise gravity (11:8.4).
11.b60.t: Space potency is individuated into the pre-energy forms of cosmic force (11:8.5)
Produced by the Paradise force organizers; responds to Paradise gravity (11:8.6)
Responds to linear gravity; threefold in the central universe, dual in the superuniverses (11:8.7)
11.b61.p: The dark gravity bodies circling Havona are neither triata nor gravita, and they show both linear and absolute gravity (11:8.7). Space potency is not subject to any form of gravity, yet it is ancestral to all organization of force, energy, and matter (11:8.8). The presence of the Unqualified Absolute is like an elastic tension of Paradise presence, which helps us grasp why everything is drawn inward toward Paradise (11:8.9).
11.b63.p: Paradise is the place of origin and the final goal of all spirit personalities (11:9.1). Yet it is not part of the universal creation, not even a real part of eternal Havona. Paradise is an eternal and exclusive existence (11:9.2).
11.b64.p: The account of its origin is the deepest passage of the paper. When the Father gave expression to his spirit self in the Eternal Son, at the same time he revealed the infinity potential of his nonpersonal self as Paradise (11:9.3).
11.b66.p: The tension between the two, met by the will of the Father and the Son, gave existence to the Conjoint Actor and the central universe (11:9.3). Paradise, then, is not Deity, nor is it conscious in any sense mortal man could understand (11:9.4). It is not ancestral to any being, and it is not a creator; it is the absolute of patterns (11:9.5).
11.b68.p: In the last paragraph the author brings out what matters most to mortals. This perfect home of the Father is the real and far-distant destiny of our immortal souls. Every God-knowing mortal who has chosen a life of doing the Father’s will has already set out on that long, long trail (11:9.8).
11.b70.p: Paper 11 shows the dwelling place of God not as a vague heaven but as a real place with shape, regions, and dimensions. There space breathes, gravity holds all things, and every energy goes out and returns. The author admits what he does not know, yet he makes one thing clear: the Father is always there, and whatever path we trace back, it leads to him. So the Isle is not merely the geography of a distant universe. It is the end of the road already being walked by everyone who has chosen to do the Father’s will.
11.b71.t: The Father is always at the center, and every circuit leads back to him
A unique Isle, material yet beyond time and space, divided into three domains
The Father’s mansions are of unimaginable scale, yet use less than one per cent of the land
A landing field and exhibit area, with land kept for creations yet to come
No personalities dwell there, yet all physical energy and force circuits begin there
Pervaded and unpervaded space breathe in turn in a two-billion-year cycle
Space is a bestowal of Paradise, and quiet zones keep the universes stable
Paradise gravity is the strand that holds all things, and energy responds in three stages
Neither Deity nor creator, yet the real destination of every God-knowing mortal
11.b73.box: God dwells not in some vague somewhere but in a real place, and that place is the end of the road already being walked by all who do the Father’s will.
12.title: The Universe of Universes
12.b0.ask: “In a universe this vast, what place do I, one single person, have?”
12.b2.p: Paper 11 showed Paradise, the center of all things. Paper 12 sketches the whole creation spread out around that center. From the first sentence the author is candid: the enormousness of the master universe staggers the concept even of his own order of being (12:0.1).
12.b3.p: Yet this paper is not meant to crush us with numbers. It explains space and time, gravity and motion in turn, and then in the seventh section it changes direction. Within this immense whole, what am I, a single part? At the end it answers: the Father is not very far from any one of us (12:7.12).
12.b6.h: 1. Space Levels of the Master Universe
12.b7.p: The universe is not an endless plane. It is an organized whole with definite dimensions. The fact that all basic energy forever swings around a curved path in obedience to Paradise gravity is proof that the universe has bounds (12:1.1).
12.b8.p: Moving outward from Paradise, six concentric ellipses — the space levels — unfold one after another (12:1.3).
12.b9.t: Not a time creation but an eternal existence: one billion perfect spheres (12:1.4, 1.10)
The creations of time — the presently organized and inhabited grand universe (12:1.5, 1.13)
A belt of activity where vast wheels of force are now turning (12:1.6, 1.14)
A region where early evidence of force manifestations has been detected (12:1.7, 1.15)
A region where only signs of a direction of revolution are observed (12:1.8)
The outer edge of the master universe (12:1.9, 1.16)
12.b10.p: Our local universe, Nebadon, is one of the newer creations in Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse, and it lies in a far-off corner near the outer border of the grand universe (12:1.12–13).
12.b11.h: 2. The Domains of the Unqualified Absolute
12.b12.p: The larger our telescopes grow, the more universes they reveal. The author says that before long no less than 375 million new galaxies will come into view (12:2.3). This vast region beyond the seven superuniverses is recognized as the domain of the Unqualified Absolute (12:2.1).
12.b13.p: What is striking is the author’s attitude. He admits that he knows little more about these regions than the astronomers of Urantia do (12:2.5). He tells us only that the energy and matter out there already equal many times that of all seven superuniverses, and that a greater creation of the future is in the making (12:2.4–5).
12.b15.p: All force and energy are subject to gravity. There are four absolute gravity circuits, and the Father acts over all of them (12:3.1).
12.b17.p: The figures from the corps of gravity researchers on Uversa are among the most intriguing parts of the paper. By comparing how much of each gravity is now in use, we can guess what is happening in outer space.
12.b18.t: Share in use in the grand universe
The other ninety-five per cent is controlling material systems beyond the organized universes (12:3.8)
The universes now growing in outer space are wholly nonspiritual (12:3.9)
Some intelligence is directing evolution out there as well (12:3.10)
12.b19.p: Only personality gravity cannot be computed. The circuit is recognized, but there is no way to measure the realities that respond to it (12:3.12). Persons cannot be measured.
12.b21.p: In the whole master universe only Paradise is absolutely stationary; everything else revolves and swings (12:4.1). On the origin of motion the author does not make a final claim. He sets out three opinions side by side.
12.b22.t: We think he initiates motion in space (12:4.3)
If he does, we cannot prove it (12:4.4)
Does not originate initial motion, but equalizes and controls the tensions it creates (12:4.5)
12.b23.p: To human eyes space seems to be nothing, yet space is real. It contains and conditions motion — it even moves (12:4.7).
12.b24.t: Space respiration, the motion of space itself (12:4.8)
The alternate directional swings of the successive space levels (12:4.9)
Motions not measured with Paradise as the base point (12:4.10)
Movement that co-ordinates all other motions (12:4.11)
12.b25.p: All seven superuniverses take part in the two-billion-year cycles of space respiration (12:4.12). The way far-off galaxies seem to fly away at tens of thousands of miles a second is not real; it is an illusion caused by angles of observation and time-space distortions (12:4.14–15).
12.b27.p: Time, too, is a bestowal of Paradise, but only indirectly. Time comes by virtue of motion and because mind is inherently aware of sequence (12:5.1). The absolute of time is eternity (12:5.2).
12.b28.t: Consciousness of sequence, motion, and a sense of duration (12:5.7)
Insight into motion Godward, the awareness of ascent to higher divinity (12:5.8)
Insight into Reality plus a consciousness of presence and an awareness of duration (12:5.9)
12.b29.p: Unspiritual animals know only the past and live in the present. Spirit-indwelt man can picture the future. Only forward-looking and progressive attitudes are personally real (12:5.10). Human personality is not merely a by-product of events in time and space; it can also act as the cosmic cause of such events (12:5.11).
12.b31.p: The stability of the universe is not gained by standing still. It is the product of balanced energies, co-operative minds, spirit overcontrol, and personality unification — and stability is always proportional to divinity (12:6.1).
12.b32.p: So the universe is highly predictable only in a quantitative sense. When matter, mind, and spirit are unified in a creature personality, the decisions of that freewill being cannot be fully predicted (12:6.5). The care of the whole, from Paradise to the outermost space level, depends on the following (12:6.8).
12.b33.t: The Architects of the Master Universe
12.b35.p: In this section the weight of the paper shifts. Mercy characterizes God’s attitude of love for the individual; impartiality motivates his attitude toward the total. The will of God does not necessarily prevail in any one person’s heart, but it does rule the universe of universes (12:7.1).
12.b36.p: The laws of God are not arbitrary commands. They are the habits of God, his way of doing things repeatedly because that is the best way (12:7.2). Yet he is not a slave to habit. Where a better way is called for, he acts in that better way — and that is the expression of a higher law, not the reversal of a lower one (12:7.3–4).
12.b37.p: The Father’s love makes each person a unique child, without duplicate in infinity and irreplaceable in all eternity (12:7.9). And because that same love goes out to everyone, love for the individual gives rise to the universal brotherhood (12:7.10).
12.b38.p: So no person can escape the benefits or the penalties that come from being related to others. The good effort of each one benefits all; the error of each one adds to the troubles of all. As the part moves, so moves the whole (12:7.11).
12.b39.p: Then comes the warmest passage of the paper. Do not let the vastness of infinity overawe or discourage you, for the Father is not very far from any one of you (12:7.12). The Father abides on Paradise, but his divine presence also dwells in the minds of men (12:7.13).
12.b41.p: “⟦Q 12:8.1|12:8.14|1:3.1⟧God is spirit,⟦/Q⟧” but Paradise is not (12:8.1). The material universe is always the arena where all spiritual activities take place. The human intellect can grasp three working levels of finite reality (12:8.9).
12.b42.t: Organized energy subject to linear gravity, except as modified by motion and conditioned by mind (12:8.10)
Organized consciousness not wholly subject to material gravity, which becomes truly liberated when modified by spirit (12:8.11)
The highest personal reality; not subject to physical gravity (12:8.12)
12.b43.p: The more spiritual — the more Godlike — a mind becomes, the less it responds to material gravity (12:8.5). Mind is the technique by which spirit realities become experiential to creatures (12:8.8), and the goal of existence of all personalities is spirit (12:8.13).
12.b44.p: In time, the body is just as real as mind or spirit. But at death, mind and spirit survive while the body does not (12:8.16).
12.b46.p: The last section comes down from cosmology to the human story. Love is the secret of beneficial association between persons, and you cannot really know a person from a single contact (12:9.2). A telephone number tells nothing about the personality of the one who has it.
12.b47.p: No mathematics or chemistry could have predicted that two atoms of hydrogen and one of oxygen would become water (12:9.3). Nor does any analysis reveal that water puts out fire (12:9.4). The whole is more than, and different from, the sum of its parts.
12.b48.p: Man has a spirit nucleus, and mind is a personal-energy system existing around that divine nucleus and working in a material environment (12:9.6). Real trouble and lasting disappointment come only when the self-concept tries to push aside the central spirit nucleus entirely and take its place.
12.b50.p: Paper 12 takes us out to the farthest edge and then brings us back into our own minds. In numbers, one person looks smaller than a speck of dust. But the Father’s love makes that speck a child without duplicate in infinity. The whole does not swallow the part; the part moves the whole. So there is no reason to feel small before such vastness. The Father is not far away, and in him we all live and move and have our being.
12.b51.t: Section
Key message
1. Space Levels of the Master Universe
The universe is not endless but one organized whole with six space levels
2. The Domains of the Unqualified Absolute
A greater creation is forming beyond, and even the author does not fully know its meaning
3. Universal Gravity
Of the four absolute circuits, only personality gravity cannot be measured
4. Space and Motion
Only Paradise stands still; space itself breathes and moves
5. Space and Time
Only forward-looking attitudes are personally real
6. Universal Overcontrol
Stability is proportional to divinity, not inertia, and free will cannot be predicted
7. The Part and the Whole
Love for each person creates universal brotherhood, and as the part moves, so moves the whole
8. Matter, Mind, and Spirit
Mind is how spirit becomes real in experience, and the goal of every personality is spirit
9. Personal Realities
Love is the secret of association, and trouble begins when the self pushes aside the spirit nucleus
12.b53.box: The universe is vast enough to swallow me, yet within it the Father’s love establishes me as one irreplaceable person.
13.title: The Sacred Spheres of Paradise
13.b0.ask: “Why do the twenty-one worlds circling closest to Paradise hold secrets that are kept forever?”
13.b2.p: In Papers 11 and 12 we saw how the eternal Isle of Paradise and the universe of universes are arranged. Now Paper 13 narrows our gaze to the space right beside Paradise. Between Paradise and the innermost circuit of Havona lie three lesser circuits, and in each circuit seven spheres revolve (13:0.1).
13.b3.p: These twenty-one worlds are eternal like Paradise, and there is neither record nor tradition of their origin (13:0.2). The Father’s spheres reflect and shed the light of the glory of the Deities; the Son’s spheres give off light without heat; and the Spirit’s spheres send spiritual illumination to the seven superuniverses (13:0.3–5). Thousands of activities unrevealed to us are going on there, and this paper offers only a fleeting glimpse of a small part of them (13:0.7).
13.b4.p: What, then, do these sacred spheres hold? And why are some of their secrets closed even to the highest beings, while one secret is opened only to us mortals?
13.b7.h: 1. The Seven Sacred Worlds of the Father
13.b8.t: Seven secret spheres — forbidden domains holding the secrets of personality
Seven luminous worlds — pure-spirit worlds where no personality may sojourn
Seven immense spheres — the executive headquarters of the Seven Master Spirits
13.b9.p: The Father’s circuit holds the only inherent personality secrets in the universe of universes, and it is the only forbidden domain concerned with personality in the central universe (13:1.1). These worlds are directed by the highest order of the Stationary Sons of the Trinity, the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy. Even the author, a Perfector of Wisdom, admits that though he is somewhat familiar with six of these worlds, he has never landed on Divinington (13:1.2).
13.b10.p: One reason these worlds are secret is that each holds a specialized manifestation of the Deities of the Trinity. It is not a personality, but a unique presence of Divinity that only the particular groups admitted to that sphere can appreciate (13:1.3). Each of the seven worlds is clearly distinct — in whose “bosom” it is, and in what secret it keeps (13:1.4–22).
13.b11.t: The bestowal and mission of Thought Adjusters
The incarnation of the divine Sons
The bosom of the Father and the Son
Trinitization — the authority to represent the Trinity
The bosom of the Father and the Spirit
The personal relation of the Infinite Spirit with certain of his higher offspring
The bosom of the Son and the Spirit
Seraphic transport, and two other mysteries
The bosom of the Father, Son, and Spirit
The evolution of an immortal soul within a mortal mind
13.b12.p: Three of these mysteries point to the three Deities. The Adjusters are a mystery of God the Father; the incarnation of the divine Sons is a mystery of God the Son; and reflectivity is a secret of God the Spirit (13:1.8, 1.10). When a Son of God is literally born of woman and becomes a Son of Man, that secret is locked up in the seventh sector of Sonarington, which no one may enter except those who have personally passed through that experience (13:1.8).
13.b13.t: A mystery of God the Father — Divinington
The incarnation of the divine Sons
A mystery of God the Son — Sonarington
A secret of God the Spirit — Spiritington
13.b14.p: The seventh world, Ascendington, is the one closest to us. It receives the pilgrims of time passing through Havona, and we will spend most of our Havona “vacations” there (13:1.21). Its secret is the mystery of the gradual building up, in the material and mortal mind, of a spiritual and potentially immortal counterpart of character and identity — the evolution of the soul (13:1.22).
13.b16.p: Remarkably, one seventh of Ascendington is forbidden to the Perfector of Wisdom, because that sector belongs to the experience of our human order alone. The secret is eventually revealed to us — but even after it is revealed, it forever remains our secret, never disclosed to any other order of beings (13:1.23).
13.b18.p: These home worlds equal Paradise in beauty and glory. They are rendezvous worlds and reunion spheres, serving as permanent cosmic addresses. Even when we are finaliters living on Paradise and serving in outer space, Ascendington will always be our home address and our home of cherished memories (13:2.1). If ascending creatures someday appear in the outer universes, it is inferred that they too will look upon Ascendington as their home (13:2.2).
13.b19.p: Status on these worlds is acquired by service as well as by nature of origin, and successive universe ages may redistribute certain groups of personalities (13:2.5). So although Creator Sons are of Father-Son origin, in this age they do not regard Vicegerington as their home. And Trinity-origin beings have their homes not on the Father’s worlds but on the Isle of Paradise near the Most Holy Sphere; they often appear on Ascendington, where they fraternize with the ascenders (13:2.3–5).
13.b20.t: Ascendington only; the other six may not be visited
After admission to the Corps of the Finality
Sonarington — except the sector of the incarnation secrets
Full access to Ascendington, relative access to five others besides Divinington
13.b21.p: We will never land on Divinington, the “⟦Q 13:1.4|13:1.11|13:1.15⟧bosom of the Father,⟦/Q⟧” yet we will surely stand again and again at the “⟦Q 13:2.7|5:2.2|21:4.4⟧right hand of the Father⟦/Q⟧” (13:2.7). We may become creature perfect even as the Father is deity perfect, but that does not mean we will know all the experiential secrets of every other order (13:2.8). All these secrets are thought to be known to the Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy, who are also related to the secrets of the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Supreme-Ultimate (13:2.9–10).
13.b22.h: 3. The Sacred Worlds of the Eternal Son
13.b23.p: The seven luminous spheres of the Eternal Son are the worlds of the seven phases of pure-spirit existence, and the source of the threefold light of Paradise and Havona. Their influence is largely confined to the central universe (13:3.1). No personality is present on these satellites; they teem with the otherwise-than-personal beings of the Eternal Son. Paradise philosophers maintain that in each Paradise cycle, about two billion years, new reserves of these beings are created there for the new universes of outer space (13:3.2).
13.b24.p: The author has never visited these worlds, and even the personalities cocreated by the Eternal Son do not go there. To one who has personality, such a world would seem empty and deserted. And high spirit personalities do not indulge in purposeless curiosity, for there is always far too much intriguing and purposeful adventure to pursue (13:3.3).
13.b25.t: Beings other than personal — no personalities
Shed light without heat on Paradise and Havona
13.b26.h: 4. The Worlds of the Infinite Spirit
13.b27.p: The seven spheres of the Infinite Spirit circle between the inner circuit of Havona and the shining spheres of the Son. They are inhabited by the offspring of the Infinite Spirit, by the trinitized sons of glorified created personalities, and by many other beings concerned with universe administration (13:4.1). From these executive spheres the Seven Master Spirits carry on all their management of the grand universe, serving as the mind-spirit balance wheel of the universe of universes (13:4.2–3).
13.b28.p: Here comes the most practical teaching of the paper. Physical presence is uniform and automatic everywhere, but experiential spiritual presence varies according to the spiritual receptivity of each mind (13:4.3–4). What decides the difference is our own choosing and our own decisions. The Deities bestow more of their presence in response to sincere desire, and withdraw when their creatures decide against them (13:4.5).
13.b29.t: Not influenced by the loyalty or disloyalty of creatures
Directly influenced by the decisions and choices of creatures
13.b31.p: Each of the seven executive worlds is assigned to one Master Spirit and serves as the Paradise headquarters of one superuniverse. Unlike the spheres of the Father or the Son, they are open to all who wish to visit and can command the means of transit (13:4.6). The author says that when he is released from assignment he often goes to one of these busy worlds to inspire his mind with the devotion and wisdom of those who know their work well and thoroughly enjoy doing it (13:4.7).
13.b33.p: Paper 13 shows us the twenty-one worlds that circle beside Paradise, and at the same time it honestly tells us how much they keep hidden. But these secrets are not walls meant to shut us out. The Creator keeps in eternal confidence the experience he shares with each creature, and one of these secrets — the evolution of the soul and its fusion with the Adjuster — belongs to us mortals alone. And the nearest divine presence is decided not on some distant sphere but in our own choices. The spirit of God comes in answer to our sincere longing and humbly yields to our decisions.
13.b34.t: The Seven Sacred Worlds of the Father
Each of the seven “bosoms” keeps a secret guarded by the Deities and their unions
Ascendington is our eternal home address; Divinington is closed forever
The Sacred Worlds of the Eternal Son
Pure-spirit worlds without personality give light and prepare new reserves
The Worlds of the Infinite Spirit
Our own choices decide how much of the spiritual presence we receive
13.b36.box: The Creator keeps forever the secrets he shares with his creatures, and the spirit of divinity humbly answers our choices.
14.title: The Central and Divine Universe
14.b0.ask: “Why does a universe perfect from the very beginning lie at the center of the evolving universes?”
14.b2.p: In Paper 13 we saw the twenty-one sacred spheres circling right beside Paradise. Paper 14 now moves out to the billion worlds that surround them — Havona, the central universe. Havona occupies the center of all creation; it is the eternal core around which the vast creations of time and space revolve (14:0.1).
14.b3.p: Havona is not the product of evolution. It is a wholly created and perfect universe. Around it swirls the endless evolutionary experiment and adventure led by the Creator Sons, who aspire to duplicate in time and reproduce in space the perfection of this pattern universe (14:0.2).
14.b4.p: How, then, is this perfect universe arranged? Who lives there, and how? And what does it mean for us, who are still evolving?
14.b8.p: From the edge of Paradise to the inner borders of the seven superuniverses lie seven space conditions and motions in turn. Quiet zones and revolving belts alternate, and among them the Havona circuits swing clockwise (14:1.1–8).
14.b9.t: The quiet midspace zones touching Paradise
The clockwise procession of the three Paradise circuits and the seven Havona circuits
A semiquiet zone separating Havona from the dark gravity bodies
The inner belt of dark gravity bodies, moving counterclockwise
A unique space zone dividing the two belts of dark gravity bodies
The outer belt of dark gravity bodies, revolving clockwise
A third semiquiet zone separating them from the innermost superuniverse circuits
14.b10.p: The billion worlds of Havona are arranged in seven concentric circuits. The innermost circuit has upwards of thirty-five million worlds and the outermost over two hundred and forty-five million, and each circuit is pervaded by one of the Seven Spirits of the Circuits (14:1.9). Physically, the Paradise circuits and the Havona circuits are one system; they are distinguished only for function and administration (14:1.10).
14.b11.p: Time is not reckoned on Paradise, but it does have meaning in Havona. The innermost circuit takes almost one thousand years to complete one revolution, and this is the Paradise-Havona standard day, the standard time of the seven superuniverses. The saying “⟦Q 14:1.12⟧A day is as a thousand years with God⟦/Q⟧” turns out to have been a truth read unwittingly (14:1.12–13).
14.b12.p: Beyond Havona, enormous dark gravity bodies that neither reflect nor absorb light form two belts that hide Havona from view. Because the two belts revolve in opposite directions, they equalize the lines of gravity and keep the central universe perfectly stable (14:1.14–15).
14.b13.t: Counterclockwise; tubular, in three circular groupings
Clockwise; arranged perpendicularly, ten thousand times higher than the inner
Enormous up-and-down wave movements and energy activities of an unknown order
14.b15.p: Spirit beings do not live on ethereal worlds but on spheres just as real as those of mortals. Havona’s substance, however, differs from that of the superuniverses (14:2.1). Superuniverse energy is twofold, with negative and positive phases; Havona energy is threefold, like the Trinity (14:2.2). Havona matter is made of exactly one thousand basic chemical elements and seven forms of energy, so that the natives of Havona have forty-nine forms of sensation (14:2.3).
14.b16.t: Twofold — by a Creator Son and a Creative Spirit
14.b17.p: So if a Urantia mortal were carried to Havona as he is, he would be deaf and blind there, able to exist only as a limited self-conscious being (14:2.4). In Havona the spirit gravity of the Son and the mind gravity of the Spirit work together to draw ascending souls toward God. The pull is not stronger there; rather, those who reach Havona are more fully spiritualized and so respond to it more fully (14:2.7–8).
14.b19.p: Everything physical or spiritual there is predictable, but mind and personal will are not. Even so, no native of Havona and no pilgrim who has entered it has ever sinned, and no ascending soul has ever been admitted too soon (14:2.9).
14.b21.p: Havona has no government. There are no courts and no legislative assemblies — only administrative direction. Here the ideals of true self-government reach their height (14:3.1). Each sphere is directed by an Eternal of Days, a Trinity-origin personality; these are not creators, but perfect administrators and teachers (14:3.3).
14.b22.p: The billion spheres are the training worlds for the natives of Paradise and Havona, and the final proving grounds for ascending creatures from the evolutionary worlds. The pilgrims land on the outermost, seventh circuit and progress inward, planet by planet and circle by circle, until they reach Paradise (14:3.4). At present only about one per cent of the planetary capacity is used for mortal ascension (14:3.5). The architecture, lighting, and embellishment are beyond imagining — yet there are real rivers and lakes on these worlds (14:3.7).
14.b24.p: There are seven basic forms of life in Havona. Each exists in three phases, each phase has seventy major divisions, and each major division has a thousand minor divisions (14:4.1). Decay and death are not part of the cycle of life in Havona; even the lower living things do not decay but only change form (14:4.9).
14.b26.p: The natives of Havona are all offspring of the Paradise Trinity. They have no creature parents and do not reproduce (14:4.10). They live meaningful lives of their own, quite apart from Paradise or the superuniverses (14:4.12). While mortal man strives to do the will of God, the Havoners in their very nature are the will of God (14:4.13).
14.b28.t: From the first circuit to the seventh
From the seventh circuit to the first
Within the worlds of a given circuit
14.b29.p: Besides the natives, Havona is home to pattern beings for every group in creation — advisers, directors, and teachers. All beings in all universes are fashioned after some order of pattern creature living on one of the billion worlds of Havona (14:4.18). A host of personalities of the Infinite Spirit also teach and minister to the ascending creatures there (14:4.20).
14.b31.p: After the short and intense test of life on Urantia, the morontia ascent, and the spiritual training of the superuniverse, we reach Havona. On its seven circuits our attainment is intellectual, spiritual, and experiential (14:5.1). The rules of Havona are not arbitrary but natural, and we will naturally enjoy doing things the way they should be done (14:5.3).
14.b32.t: Where new arrivals are first received
After attaining identity comprehension of one’s superuniverse Master Spirit
After attaining a realization of Supremacy
Acceptance into the service of Paradise — then on to the Corps of the Finality
14.b33.p: Even the term “⟦Q 14:5.4⟧circles of progress⟦/Q⟧” in the human mind comes from this arrangement (14:5.4). No two of Havona’s billion worlds are alike, for each was developed according to the plans of its resident Eternal of Days (14:5.6). So monotony is not a part of the Havona career; each world is a veritable university of surprises (14:5.9).
14.b34.p: Love of adventure, curiosity, and dread of monotony were not given to us merely to annoy us. They are there to suggest that death is only the beginning of an endless career of adventure. On earth these urges must often be restrained and often meet disappointment, but they will be fully realized in the long ages to come (14:5.10–11).
14.b35.h: 6. The Purpose of the Central Universe
14.b36.p: The activities of Havona fall broadly into three kinds: Havonal, Paradisiacal, and ascendant-finite (14:6.1–4). The author describes what this perfect creation gives to each of seven orders of universe intelligence (14:6.5).
14.b37.t: Supreme parental satisfaction in the adoration of perfect creatures
The first and eternally final demonstration that the Son is the Word of the Father
A rehearsal stage for the ministry of mercy, and a mind laboratory
A finished portrayal of the future perfection of the Supreme
A training ground for universe creation, and the pattern to follow
Prepersonal training and the mind patterns for their creatures
The pre-Paradise training goal and the portal to God
14.b38.p: For mortals, Havona is where we attain the Supreme Being, and it stands as the portal to Paradise and God attainment (14:6.38). Yet that is not the end. Havona is also the starting place from which finaliters will someday set out to explore the infinity of the Father, and it has the capacity to serve as a training universe for every type of created being in future universe ages (14:6.40–41).
14.b40.p: Paper 14 shows that at the center of the evolving universes lies a universe perfect from the beginning. Havona is a real world woven of threefold energy, the height of self-government, running without government and without sin. Its perfection is not far removed from us. It is the pattern every Creator Son seeks to achieve in his own universe, the model after which every being is made, and the school through which we ascending mortals will walk, circuit by circuit. Because no two of its billion worlds are alike, there is no monotony on that road, and the curiosity and love of adventure now held back in us will be gloriously satisfied there. Havona is a destination, and at the same time the starting point of an eternal adventure.
14.b41.t: A billion worlds revolve in seven circuits, guarded by the dark gravity bodies
A perfect, stable universe of threefold energy where sin has never appeared
The height of self-government — administration without government — and the final proving ground of ascenders
The natives, offspring of the Trinity, are in their very nature the will of God
On the road inward through seven circuits, there is no monotony
The Purpose of the Central Universe
Havona is the pattern for every order, and for mortals the portal to God
14.b43.box: Havona is the pattern of every evolving universe, and for us it is the portal to God and the starting point of an eternal adventure.
15.title: The Seven Superuniverses
15.b0.ask: “Urantia is one of seven trillion worlds — where in the universe is it, and how is it governed?”
15.b2.p: In Paper 14 we saw Havona, the perfect central universe. Paper 15 now moves beyond Havona to the seven superuniverses that circle on the first space level. As far as the Paradise Trinity is concerned, these seven are the only inhabited universes outside Havona. The whole creation is like one gigantic wheel: the hub is the Isle of Paradise, the seven spokes are the radiations of the Seven Master Spirits, and the rim is the outer region of the grand universe (15:0.1).
15.b3.p: This sevenfold plan of organization was formulated early in the materialization of the universal creation, and its rulers are rightly called Ancients of Days (15:0.2). The author, a Universal Censor, says that we must first understand the physical structure of the superuniverses before we can grasp the meaning of their spiritual government (15:0.3).
15.b4.p: Where, then, is our Urantia in this vast system? And who governs these superuniverses, and how?
15.b8.p: Our world may seem to be plunging blindly into uncharted space, but in fact the seven superuniverses are circling Paradise in an orderly procession along a great ellipse. Our local universe, too, is following a well-known counterclockwise course (15:1.1–3). Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse to which we belong, not long ago turned the southeastern bend and is now moving along the long and nearly straight northern path (15:1.5).
15.b10.p: Only the Universal Father knows the exact location and number of the inhabited worlds. The figures the author gives are approximations, offered to help us sense the immensity of the material creation (15:2.1, 2.25). A superuniverse is organized in seven levels, from the system up to the grand universe (15:2.3–9).
15.b11.t: Three Most Highs; a Faithful of Days
A Creator Son; a Union of Days
The Seven Master Spirits, from Paradise
15.b14.p: Nearly all the stars visible to the naked eye from Urantia belong to Orvonton, and the Milky Way is the central nucleus of Orvonton (15:3.1). The rotational center of our minor sector lies in the star cloud of Sagittarius, and our solar system sits in one arm of the onetime Andronover nebula (15:3.5–6). Star observation is difficult because many layers of revolving motion overlap and create illusions (15:3.7).
15.b15.t: The solar system around the nucleus of the former Andronover nebula
The Andronover family around the center of the Nebadon star cloud
The Nebadon star cloud around the Sagittarius center of its minor sector
The one hundred minor sectors around their major sector
The ten major sectors around Uversa
The seven superuniverses around Paradise and Havona
15.b17.p: The Paradise force organizers transmute space potency into primordial force and set in motion tremendous cyclones of force that become nebulae. These nebulae are the mother wheels that give birth to suns and systems (15:4.2, 4.4). Energy is not organized by nebulae but distributed universally, so each local universe holds exactly one one-hundred-thousandth of a superuniverse’s total energy (15:4.6). When you look at Andromeda, the author suggests, remember that the light you see left those suns almost one million years ago (15:4.7).
15.b19.p: Most of the suns and planets of a superuniverse come from nebular wheels (15:5.1). By origin, the majority fall into ten groups, and our own solar system was born of a gravity explosion (15:5.2–13).
15.b20.t: A nebula condenses into many rings
Suns thrown off the heated mother wheels
Formed by tidal eruptions — the origin of our solar system
Matter thrown off by a fast-spinning sun
A star past its critical size splits in two
A large planet draws in its neighboring worlds
Built up slowly from space matter
Dark islands whose energy is spent
Collision debris becomes the nucleus of new planets
Worlds built to plan, such as Salvington and Uversa
15.b22.p: Except for the architectural spheres, all space bodies have an evolutionary origin. This does not mean they came into being by divine fiat; it means God’s creative acts unfolded by a time-space technique through the work of many intelligences (15:6.7).
15.b23.t: Over a thousand states and stages; accelerators of energy circulation
Dead suns and other dark masses; balance wheels that hold systems steady
Comets and meteors — a comet’s tail shows that light has weight
Including the inhabited worlds; cold worlds are best suited for life
15.b24.p: Orvonton is lighted and warmed by more than ten trillion suns, yet not one cool planet in forty is habitable by beings of our order. In size, density, and location, Urantia is in many respects ideal for human habitation (15:6.10, 6.15).
15.b26.p: The superuniverse governments are seated on architectural spheres built for a special purpose; these headquarters worlds are lighted by a sun that gives light without heat and warmed by energy currents (15:7.1). The Orvonton year is about eight and one fifth of our years (15:7.2). As ascenders pass through the headquarters worlds, they move into ever greater beauty and glory (15:7.3).
15.b27.t: Seven worlds with the seven mansion worlds — man’s first home after death
Seventy satellites — socializing culture and training
Seven higher universities — spiritual training before the flight to Havona
15.b29.p: The superuniverse headquarters, power centers, and physical controllers regulate the balance of energy (15:8.1–2). When mass builds up too much, a collision among the dead giants of space converts it back into energy and restores the balance (15:8.6). The farther we go from Paradise, the more unpredictable the phenomena become — a sign that there is a universal overcontrol of all things (15:8.8–9).
15.b32.p: The Paradise circuits — the personality gravity of the Father, the spiritual gravity of the Son, the mind gravity of the Conjoint Actor, and the material gravity of the Isle — pervade the superuniverses. Besides these, superuniverse circuits and local universe circuits function on their own (15:9.1–2).
15.b33.t: The unifying intelligence circuit of a Master Spirit
The reflective-service circuit of the Reflective Spirits
The secret circuits of the Mystery Monitors
The intercommunion of the Eternal Son with his Paradise Sons
The flash presence of the Infinite Spirit
The broadcasts of Paradise, the space reports of Havona
The energy circuits of the power centers and physical controllers
The bestowal spirit — the Spirit of Truth, the spirit of Michael
The Universe Mother Spirit — the Holy Spirit
The intelligence-ministry circuit of the adjutant mind-spirits
15.b34.p: For a local universe to join the superuniverse confederation, it must meet two requirements: physical stability and spiritual loyalty. Nebadon has not yet qualified, but the superuniverse government earnestly desires its admission and lends every possible assistance (15:9.15–18).
15.b36.p: Each superuniverse is presided over jointly by three Ancients of Days, and its executive branch is made up of seven groups (15:10.3). The first four are of direct Trinity origin; the last three are glorified ascendant mortals. The perfected children of the evolutionary worlds have thus been brought into the superuniverse government itself (15:10.11–12).
15.b38.p: The superuniverses keep no ambassadors with one another; they are completely isolated, knowing of each other’s affairs only through the Paradise clearinghouse of the Seven Master Spirits. This isolation will last until the sovereignty of the Supreme Being is more completely realized (15:10.23).
15.b40.p: On Uversa the autocracy of perfection and the democracy of evolution meet face to face. The executive branch comes from the realms of perfection; the legislative branch springs from the evolutionary universes (15:11.1). Each local universe admitted to the councils elects a representative to each of the seven houses, chosen from the ascending graduates waiting on Uversa for transport to Havona (15:11.2). There has never been a disagreement between the executives and the assembly — proof that evolutionary beings can truly reach the heights of perfected wisdom (15:11.3).
15.b42.p: The superuniverse also has a judicial branch, but it has no separate personnel; the executive personalities share its roles (15:12.1). The Sons of the local universes can decree the survival of mortal man, but only the Ancients of Days may judge the issues of eternal life and death. Their rulings are always unanimous, and there is no appeal from them (15:12.2–4).
15.b43.t: An Ancient of Days, a Perfector of Wisdom, or a Divine Counselor
Portraying the attitude of the higher government
A commission of Those without Name and Number and members chosen from the assembly
15.b45.p: The major and minor sectors also have governments led by Trinity personalities. The major sectors deal chiefly with intellectual status; the minor sectors with physical control and co-ordination (15:13.2, 13.4). Reports of observation travel upward from the constellations and local universes through the minor and major sectors to the Ancients of Days. The local system headquarters, however, have no Trinity representatives (15:13.6).
15.b46.t: Intellectual status; sorting and reporting administrative matters
15.b48.p: Each of the seven superuniverses gives fullest expression to one major purpose (15:14.1). Orvonton is renowned for justice tempered by mercy and power conditioned by patience; it is a universe demonstration of love and mercy. Because the purposes of the other six superuniverses are being brought together here, it has been conjectured that God the Supreme will someday rule the seven superuniverses from Uversa (15:14.2–3).
15.b49.t: Universe number 84 of Ensa (capital Uminor the third)
Minor sector number 3 of Splandon (headquarters Umajor the fifth)
Major sector number 5 of Orvonton (headquarters Uversa)
15.b52.p: Paper 15 is not written to overwhelm us with the size of the universe. After showing seven trillion worlds, ten trillion suns, layer upon layer of revolving motion, and an intricate structure of government, the author gives Urantia’s exact address and registry number. We are not a lost planet but a world moving along an ordered path, under the care of a government shared by Trinity personalities and glorified ascenders. And Orvonton, the superuniverse to which we belong, demonstrates love and mercy. We are one of an almost infinite family of worlds, yet our world is administered as precisely and fostered as lovingly as if it were the only one.
